rationale: Start with a broad mid-strength scouting gradient at moderate temperature to maximize the chance all 10 compounds elute while revealing the overall retention window and any severe crowding. This first run should map whether the mixture is generally early, late, or broadly spread so later injections can optimize slope and window.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only way to improve CRF is to bring the last peak earlier than 12.7 min while preserving the weakest pair around rows 6–7. Shortening the gradient one step is the cleanest exploitation move because it should compress the run and reduce t_last without changing the selectivity window much.

We are very close to the ideal 10 min cutoff, and the weakest pair still has comfortable margin at R = 1.83. Reduce tG by one more step to try to pull the last peak under 10 min while checking whether the critical 6–7 pair remains at or above 1.5.

At 14 min the run is fast enough, so the remaining task is to restore the slightly under-resolved 6–7 pair without pushing the last peak back above 10 min. Dropping temperature one step may improve selectivity around the critical pair while likely keeping t_last close enough to the cutoff to preserve or improve CRF.

Lowering temperature worsened selectivity by creating a new severe 5–6 overlap, so test the opposite direction from the near-optimal 14 min method. A 5 C increase may restore full resolution or at least improve the critical cluster while keeping the last peak safely under 10 min.

Temperature changes hurt the crowded middle cluster, so keep T at 40 C and instead widen the gradient window at the weakly retained end by lowering phi0 one step. This should spread the early/mid peaks, especially the critical 5–7 region, while likely keeping the last peak under 10 min because phi1 and tG are unchanged.

Changing phi0 did not quite recover the critical 6–7 pair, so now test a slightly stronger gradient end while keeping the same slope region near the crowded cluster as close as possible. Raising phi1 one step may pull the last peak a bit earlier and can alter selectivity enough to nudge the weak pair back toward full credit.

The critical 6–7 pair gets worse as the gradient is effectively made steeper/stronger, so probe the opposite direction by lowering phi1 one step from the near-best 14 min, 40 C method. This should shallow the gradient through the crowded region and may lift that pair above 1.5 while hopefully keeping t_last under 10 min.

You have reached the maximum CRF, so now test whether an even shorter method can keep all pairs at R >= 1.5 while moving the last peak to 10 min or less. Shortening tG one step from the successful 0.10–0.85, 14 min method is the most direct way to see if the optimum can be made more robustly fast.

The successful method sits right on the resolution boundary, and shortening tG failed by compressing the 6–7 pair too much. Raise phi0 one step while keeping phi1 and tG fixed to narrow the gradient window from the low-organic side; this may shift the crowded mid-region selectivity enough to preserve full resolution while pulling the last peak slightly earlier than the current best.

The move to phi0 = 0.15 improved both t_last and the critical 6–7 resolution, so continue in the same direction while staying on the winning phi1 and tG. Another increase in phi0 may further shorten the run yet still keep the weakest pair above 1.5.

phi0 = 0.15 is the best start point so far, and lowering phi1 from 0.90 to 0.85 improved the critical 6–7 pair. Test one more step lower in phi1 at the same phi0 and tG to see whether the crowded region gains enough extra resolution while still keeping the last peak within 10 min.

The best region is around phi0 0.10–0.15, phi1 0.85, but 12 min at 40 C under-resolved the 6–7 pair while 14 min at 35 C shifted selectivity strongly. Combining the shorter 12 min gradient with a 5 C lower temperature may recover separation in the critical cluster while keeping the last peak comfortably below 10 min.

The two best methods are both at 14 min and 40 C, with phi0 = 0.10 or 0.15 and phi1 = 0.85, so the optimum is already bracketed. Run a slightly longer 16 min version at the best composition window to confirm added robustness and map how much resolution margin is gained in the critical 6–7 pair for only a modest time increase.

The best region is clearly centered at phi0 = 0.10–0.15, tG = 14, T = 40, and the key tradeoff is the 6–7 pair versus retention of the last peak. Test phi1 = 0.90 at phi0 = 0.15 to complete the local map around the current optimum and confirm whether 0.85 is indeed the best upper bound.

Both winning methods suggest the optimum lies on a narrow ridge near phi1 = 0.85; lowering phi1 at phi0 = 0.15 improved resolution but pushed the last peak just past 10 min. Testing phi1 = 0.80 with phi0 = 0.10 checks whether the slightly lower start composition can recover enough speed to keep full resolution and still stay at or below the 10 min cutoff.

With two CRF-1.000 methods already found, the remaining value is understanding robustness around the current best composition window. Testing 45 C at the best method will show whether a modest temperature increase can preserve full resolution while providing a faster, potentially more margin-rich variant around the 10 min limit.

Temperature increases and decreases have both produced strong selectivity changes, so with budget left it is worth bracketing the best method further on the low-temperature side. A 30 C run at the current best composition tests whether the severe temperature sensitivity can create an alternate fully resolved solution with acceptable last-peak time.

The best methods are both at phi1 = 0.85, tG = 14, T = 40, and changing phi0 has shown a nonmonotonic effect on the critical 6–7 pair. Test the remaining lower phi0 point at this winning phi1 to complete the local map and check whether a broader low-end window can match full resolution while staying near the 10 min target.

With the local composition map essentially complete and two CRF-1.000 methods already secured, use remaining injections to test if a shorter run can be rescued by selectivity changes rather than by gradient shape alone. Although 45 C was harmful at 14 min, combining it with tG = 12 probes a different balance where faster elution is already achieved and only the critical cluster needs to respond favorably.

The best chemistry is clearly near phi1 = 0.85 and tG = 14, but temperature effects are highly nonmonotonic and have not been tested at the coldest setting for the winning composition. Use one remaining bracket point at 25 C to fully characterize whether an alternate selectivity regime exists, while retaining the already identified CRF-1.000 methods as the fallback optimum.

With the optimum already achieved, use the remaining injections to map the short-gradient failure boundary at lower temperature around the best composition. This run tests whether 12 min can ever be rescued on the cold side, complementing the strongly unfavorable 12 min/35 C and 12 min/45 C results.

The 14 min methods at 35 C were poor, but a slightly shallower gradient may relieve the severe crowding that appears at lower temperature while still staying near the successful composition window. This final low-temperature check helps define whether the cold-selectivity regime can be made acceptable by reducing slope rather than changing composition.

Only two injections remain and the optimum at 40 C is already secured, so use one to complete the temperature bracket at the same composition and longer gradient tested at 35 C. This checks whether the high-temperature regime at shallower slope behaves differently enough to rescue the critical cluster or confirms that 40 C is the unique best temperature zone.

Use the final injection to extend the temperature map one more step above 45 C at the best composition, confirming whether the sharp deterioration with heating continues monotonically and reinforcing 40 C as the optimum. The best achievable CRF is already secured at 1.000, so this last run is for final boundary definition rather than improvement.
